sections.heading: How to Play Restoration
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Restoration"][color=c7]Restoration Shaman Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]

Restoration Shaman is a very straightforward spec. Your focus will be on getting as much value as you can out of the short cooldowns and properly picking targets for your [spell=61295]s and filler casts. The basics are simple but there is room for optimization once you start getting comfortable with the kit. These are the most important things to keep in mind:

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=spell_nature_riptide size=medium type=round color=c7 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td]
        [b][color=c7]Pick Your Targets Correctly:[/color][/b] Effects like [spell=382194], [spell=200076], [spell=382039], and [spell=462424] greatly benefit from having as many [spell=61295]s active as possible so you should always aim to put Riptide on people that don't already have it. [spell=77226] and our casted heals being directly targeted also means that correctly picking people that need the most healing and are at the lowest health percentage will increase the value of everything you do.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=spell_shaman_unleashweapon_life size=medium type=round color=c7 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c7]Use Your Short Cooldowns On Cooldown:[/color][/b] Restoration Shaman has a wide list of short cooldown spells that do a variety of different things, but they all have in common that the best way to use them is to press them early and often if any healing is needed. [spell=73685], [spell=73920], [spell=444995], [spell=462486], [spell=378081], [spell=443454], and [spell=5394] and its [spell=1267068] procs all are more valuable if you use them as many times as possible during combat and focus on not missing out on casts of them.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_shaman_watershield size=medium type=round color=c7 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c7]Manage Your Mana:[/color][/b] The amount of mana you use can vary a lot depending on what spells you choose to cast outside of cooldowns: [spell=77472] is very cheap but only heals a single target and is a bit more likely to overheal while [spell=1064] is much more expensive but spreads the healing across multiple target picked in the best possible way. How much do you value each of these things can vary depending on the content you're doing and for how long you need to keep healing without running out of mana. Talents like [spell=16196] and [spell=1253093] can aleviate issues but at the cost of losing other alternatives. Pick the correct tool for the job at any given moment and understand the flow of your mana so you can keep healing for as long as it is needed.[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]
[center][cta-button guide=32734 icon=spell_nature_healingwavelesser]Restoration Shaman Starter Guide[/cta-button][/center]

sections.heading: Rotation Priority
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="Rotation Priority"][icon name=spell_nature_healingwavelesser type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon] Best Restoration Shaman Rotation[/h2]

The priority focuses on three things: Using the short cooldowns as much as possible, properly utilizing all the short buffs you generate, and balancing [spell=77472] and [spell=1064] to maximize healing while optimizing mana.

Below, we break down the main priority lists for Restoration Shaman: Raid Healing and Mythic+ Healing.

[wrapper width=70%][center][box border=true]
	[center][large][b][color=white]Hero Talent Master Switches[/color][/b][/large]
	[pad]
	You can use the master switches below to flip the [b][i]entire page's[/i][/b] options to your selected choice.[/center]
	[wrapper width=95%]
		[grid width=100% column-width=250 align=centered]
			[display-option="totemic" radio="Hero" icon=inv_ability_totemicshaman_surgingtotem checked]Totemic[/display-option][display-option="farseer" radio="Hero" icon=ability_racial_ancestralcall]Farseer[/display-option]
		[/grid]
	[/wrapper]
[/box][/center][/wrapper]
[br]
[tabs name="Rotations" uniform=true]

    [tab name="Raid Healing" icon=inv_achievement_raid_darkwell]
        [h3 toc="Raid Healing" type=bar][color=c7] Best Restoration Shaman Raid Healing Rotation[/color][/h3]
        [pad]
        On raids mana can be a concern so proper pacing of your [spell=1064] casts is important to make sure you can keep healing for the whole encounter. Your short cooldowns are very efficient and should be prioritized above filler casts as long as doing so wouldn't make you waste some of the buffs they apply.
        [pad]

        [span display-options="farseer|totemic"]With [span display-options="farseer"][symbol=wow-hero-talent-farseer] [color=necrolord]Farseer[/color][/span][span display-options="totemic"][symbol=wow-hero-talent-totemic] [color=venthyr]Totemic[/color][/span] selected, the priority is as follows:[/span]

        [div display-options="!(farseer)&!(totemic)"]
        [center][box border=true]
        [b][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-legendary-available] Please select a Hero Talent option to generate a Single Target priority[/b]
        [/box][/center]
        [/div]

Anywhere you see the [span class=tip tooltip=NotesHighlight][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span] icon, you can hover over it for additional notes.[/i][/small][/center]
            [/box][/center]
            [/wrapper]

            [h3 type=bar toc=false]Normal Priority[/h3]
            [div display-options="farseer"]
                [ol]
                    [li]Use all your [spell=1267068] procs [span class=tip tooltip=StormstreamProcs][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
                    [li]Keep [spell=61295] on cooldown [span class=tip tooltip=RiptideTargets][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
                    [li]Use [spell=443454] [span class=tip tooltip=SwiftnessCooldown][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
                    [li]Cast [spell=73685] [span class=tip tooltip=UnleashPrio][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
                    [li]Maintain [spell=73920] [span class=tip tooltip=FarseerRain][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
                    [li]Keep [spell=5394] on cooldown [span class=tip tooltip=FarseerHst][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
                    [li]Cast [spell=1064] or [spell=77472] [span class=tip tooltip=FillerSelection][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
                [/ol]

                [h3 type=bar toc=false]Stormstream Totem Usage[/h3]

One of your biggest sources of healing is [spell=1267068] and the vast majority of the procs will come from using [spell=443454]. You can also get a proc every time you cast [spell=61295] but these will be somewhat rare and you can't depend on them.

It is important to know that the buff that lets you cast [spell=1267068] lasts 60 seconds, so you don't need to use them immediately after you get it. [span display-options=farseer]It can be a good decision to save your Stormstreams for a bit to better line them up with incoming damage. As the cooldown of [spell=443454] is only 30 seconds you can infinitely refresh the [spell=1267068] buff to never let it expire, but the maximum amount of stacks you can have is two. If you don't need extra healing right now but will do so in 30 seconds or one minute you should keep using [spell=443454] and saving the [spell=1267068]s to use them all at the same time when they would get the most value. Do note that you will miss out on casts of [spell=5394] doing this but because the spell is fairly low value for [symbol=wow-hero-talent-farseer] [color=necrolord]Farseer[/color] this is acceptable.[/span][span display-options=totemic]The maximum amount of [spell=1267068] stacks you can have is two, getting a proc from [spell=61295] before spending the one from Swiftness will let you cast two of them back to back, however trying to delay casting [spell=1267068] means you miss out on [spell=5394] casts which as [symbol=wow-hero-talent-totemic] [color=venthyr]Totemic[/color] you really don't want to do. [b]While you don't need to spend your procs immediately, you are heavily incentivized to do so as soon as possible.[/b][/span]

[h3 type=bar toc=false]Chain Heal vs Healing Wave[/h3]
[pad]
Your selection of [spell=1064] or [spell=77472] to fill all time not using cooldowns comes down to how many targets need healing and how much mana do you have available. Chain Heal is considerably stronger but costs significantly more mana, while Healing Wave is still very good and also very cheap. [b]You should use [spell=1064] as much as possible as mana allows if aoe healing is needed, and [spell=77472] if you need to do single-target healing or need to conserve mana.[/b] This same decision applies during [spell=114052], the spells are considerably stronger during it but their use cases remain the same: Chain Heal does much more healing spread across several targets, while Healing Wave costs zero mana and is better at single or two target healing.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]Ascendance Sequence[/h3]
[pad]

During [spell=114052] your [spell=1064] and [spell=77472] become way stronger and you want to cast them as much as possible. To maximize the healing you do for the duration of the buff you want to do some preparation steps before entering into Ascendance. You want to make sure to have two stacks of [spell=51564] by using all your available [spell=61295]s and to cast [span display-options=farseer][spell=73685] and [spell=73920][/span][span display-options=totemic][spell=444995][/span] right before pressing the cooldown. [span display-options=farseer]Once inside of it you want to cast your chosen spell once to consume the [spell=73685] buff before using [spell=443454]. Using Swiftness before this point would make you waste the cast time reduction from Unleash Life as the spell would be instant but still consume it.[/span][span display-options=totemic]During Ascendance you want to use all your available [spell=5394]s and [spell=1267068]s, as these will cast instant free [spell=1064]s from [spell=445034]. Totems have a lower global cooldown so using them this way means you can fit more total Chain Heals for the duration of the Ascendance.[/span]

After that, simply spend all the remaining time during Ascendance casting your healing spells as many times as you can.

                    [li]Use [spell=378081] [span class=tip tooltip=SwiftnessCooldown][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
                    [li]Maintain [spell=444995] [span class=tip tooltip=SurgingTotem][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
                    [li]Keep [spell=5394] on cooldown [span class=tip tooltip=TotemicHst][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
                    [li]Cast [spell=1064] or [spell=77472] [span class=tip tooltip=FillerSelection][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
                [/ol]

                [h3 type=bar toc=false]Stormstream Totem Usage[/h3]

One of your biggest sources of healing is [spell=1267068] and the vast majority of the procs will come from using [spell=378081]. You can also get a proc every time you cast [spell=61295] but these will be somewhat rare and you can't depend on them.

It is important to know that the buff that lets you cast [spell=1267068] lasts 60 seconds, so you don't need to use them immediately after you get it. [span display-options=farseer]It can be a good decision to save your Stormstreams for a bit to better line them up with incoming damage. As the cooldown of [spell=443454] is only 30 seconds you can infinitely refresh the [spell=1267068] buff to never let it expire, but the maximum amount of stacks you can have is two. If you don't need extra healing right now but will do so in 30 seconds or one minute you should keep using [spell=443454] and saving the [spell=1267068]s to use them all at the same time when they would get the most value. Do note that you will miss out on casts of [spell=5394] doing this but because the spell is fairly low value for [symbol=wow-hero-talent-farseer] [color=necrolord]Farseer[/color] this is acceptable.[/span][span display-options=totemic]The maximum amount of [spell=1267068] stacks you can have is two, getting a proc from [spell=61295] before spending the one from Swiftness will let you cast two of them back to back, however trying to delay casting [spell=1267068] means you miss out on [spell=5394] casts which as [symbol=wow-hero-talent-totemic] [color=venthyr]Totemic[/color] you really don't want to do. [b]While you don't need to spend your procs immediately, you are heavily incentivized to do so as soon as possible.[/b][/span]

[h3 type=bar toc=false]Chain Heal vs Healing Wave[/h3]
[pad]
Your selection of [spell=1064] or [spell=77472] to fill all time not using cooldowns comes down to how many targets need healing and how much mana do you have available. Chain Heal is considerably stronger but costs significantly more mana, while Healing Wave is still very good and also very cheap. [b]You should use [spell=1064] as much as possible as mana allows if aoe healing is needed, and [spell=77472] if you need to do single-target healing or need to conserve mana.[/b] This same decision applies during [spell=114052], the spells are considerably stronger during it but their use cases remain the same: Chain Heal does much more healing spread across several targets, while Healing Wave costs zero mana and is better at single or two target healing.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]Ascendance Sequence[/h3]
[pad]

During [spell=114052] your [spell=1064] and [spell=77472] become way stronger and you want to cast them as much as possible. To maximize the healing you do for the duration of the buff you want to do some preparation steps before entering into Ascendance. You want to make sure to have two stacks of [spell=51564] by using all your available [spell=61295]s and to cast [span display-options=farseer][spell=73685] and [spell=73920][/span][span display-options=totemic][spell=444995][/span] right before pressing the cooldown. [span display-options=farseer]Once inside of it you want to cast your chosen spell once to consume the [spell=73685] buff before using [spell=378081]. Using Swiftness before this point would make you waste the cast time reduction from Unleash Life as the spell would be instant but still consume it.[/span][span display-options=totemic]During Ascendance you want to use all your available [spell=5394]s and [spell=1267068]s, as these will cast instant free [spell=1064]s from [spell=445034]. Totems have a lower global cooldown so using them this way means you can fit more total Chain Heals for the duration of the Ascendance.[/span]

After that, simply spend all the remaining time during Ascendance casting your healing spells as many times as you can.

[rotation-timeline]
    [rt-step=61295 text='All Charges']
    [rt-step=73685 display-options=farseer]
    [rt-step=444995 display-options=totemic]
    [rt-step=73920 display-options=farseer]
    [rt-step=114052]
    [rt-branch tooltip='HealingType']
        [rt-step=77472 display-options=farseer]
        [rt-step=378081]
        [rt-step=77472 start end]
    [/rt-branch]
    [rt-step=1064 display-options=farseer]
    [rt-step=5394 display-options=totemic text='All available']
    [rt-step=378081]
    [rt-step=1267068 display-options=totemic]
    [rt-step=1064 start end]
[/rotation-timeline]

[tooltip name=HealingType]If you need to heal a specific single target then you would cast Healing Wave. Any situation with at least three targets injured favors Chain Heal.[/tooltip]

            [/div]
        [/div]
    [/wrapper]
    [/tab]

sections.heading: Pre-Combat Check Before any combat happens, it is important for Restoration Shamans to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content. Buff yours
sections.body:
[h2 toc=false type=bar]Pre-Combat Check[/h2]
        Before any combat happens, it is important for Restoration Shamans to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.
        [center][wrapper width=800px][box]
            [ul]
                [li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Buff yourself -[/b] [color=q0][spell=52127], [spell=974], and [spell=382021] should always be active on yourself. [spell=1270350] helps with this and [spell=1217622] can make it so you only have to re-apply them every hour unless you die[/color][/li]
                [li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Cast Group Buffs -[/b] [color=q0]Make sure [spell=462854] is active on all the group and that someone has your second [spell=974][/color][/li]
                [li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Don't Forget Your Consumables -[/b] [color=q0]Food and flasks are an easy way to increase your throughput for just a bit of gold. Vantus and Augment runes are a more expensive one. And don't forget to bring water with you so you can restore mana when out of combat[/color][/li]
            [/ul]
        [/box][/wrapper][/center]
    [/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=c7][icon name=spell_nature_healingwavelesser type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon] Restoration Shaman Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]

Restoration has three major healing cooldowns in its talent tree, two of which share a choice node so at any given moment you will have access to two of them. Our cooldowns range from very simple to somewhat complex and possibly convoluted; here we will cover them in depth and explain what they do and how to use them. You also have access to a couple of minor cooldowns that are still very important for optimal gameplay.

[pad]
[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]
    [tab name="Ascendance" icon=spell_fire_elementaldevastation]
        [h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=spell_fire_elementaldevastation type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon][color=shaman] Ascendance [/color][/h3]

        Newly reworked going into Midnight, [spell=114052] works by enhancing your abilities for a short duration. These are the specific effects:
        [ul]
            [li]On cast, all injured allies within 20 yards will get healed. The amount of healing is fixed and gets split evenly between the targets.[/li]
            [li]Your casts of [spell=77472] will always be critical strikes and also heal a second ally for 50% the amount.[/li]
            [li]Your [spell=1064]s will bounce up to three additional times and the reduction per jump is down to 10% from the normal 30%.[/li]
            [li]Both [spell=77472] and [spell=1064] cost 25% less mana.[/li]
        [/ul]

        The lower reduction on [spell=1064] jumps is a very strong effect and combined with the reduced mana cost it makes Chain Heal an incredibly strong ability. [spell=77472] is still preferable if you only need to heal one or two targets and it is effectively mana free. Do note that the same player can't be healed twice by different bounces of the same [spell=1064] so during M+ the extra jumps won't help you at all but the jump reduction still makes the spell much better than normally.

        Each hit of [spell=77472] and [spell=1064] can proc [spell=16196] which means Ascendance in combination with it is very good for mana recovery. The guaranteed critical strikes on Healing Wave mean you will proc Resurgence on every cast and the second smaller hit also counts as it own cast so you will get two procs of the mana recovery effect every time you use the spell. This means you can effectively recover more mana than what you spend while casting Healing Wave over and over during Ascendance.

        The healing that Chain Heal can do during Ascendance is almost unmatched in raids, making Ascendance one of the strongest healer cooldowns in the game right now.
        [pad]
    [/tab]

    [tab name="Spirit Link Totem" icon=spell_shaman_spiritlink]
        [h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=spell_shaman_spiritlink type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon][color=shaman] Spirit Link Totem [/color][/h3]

        [spell=98008] is a damage reduction cooldown, meaning the best way to get value out of it is to use it right [b]before[/b] the group takes a big hit of damage. Aiming it at the floor will cover a medium-sized area where every friendly player inside takes 10% reduced damage and redistributes their health every second to keep everyone at the same percentage.

        It is a very good tool to keep your group alive through very high damage windows, as everyone will take reduced damage and players with weaker defensives that end up at lower health will get healed back up by the redistribution. You can also use it as a single-target emergency cooldown if someone is about to die and you don't have any other tool to react in time, Spirit Link will instantly get them back to very high health by taking away some from the healthier players around them.

        It is important to remember that the redistribution effect doesn't generate any healing. Every time it gets someone's health up, someone else's health has to go down.

        Using the redistribution effect to get a player's health back up quickly to a safe level after taking damage is still very good and can save lives, but using the spell this way means you get no value out of the damage reduction. Some level of proactivity is recommended to get maximum value.

        If you talent into [spell=462383], the damage reduction goes up to 15% and everyone inside the area of the totem will get healed one second after you drop it.
        [pad]
    [/tab]

    [tab name="Healing Tide Totem" icon=ability_shaman_healingtide]
        [h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_shaman_healingtide type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon][color=shaman] Healing Tide Totem [/color][/h3]

        This is the simplest cooldown in the Restoration kit. [spell=108280] will pulse several times over 10 seconds and heal all your allies within 40 yards. The healing is reduced beyond 5 targets, so the ability will heal each target more during dungeons than in raids. You can either reduce its cooldown with [spell=462440] or increase its duration, granting extra haste with [spell=462443].

        While playing [symbol=wow-hero-talent-totemic] [b][color=venthyr]Totemic[/color][/b], Healing Tide gains extra effects: a big increase from [spell=445035], a free [spell=1064] when you use it from [spell=445034], and the ability to apply [spell=382021] every time it heals from [spell=1260874]. All make it a much more attractive choice for [symbol=wow-hero-talent-totemic] [b][color=venthyr]Totemic[/color][/b] than [symbol=wow-hero-talent-farseer] [b][color=necrolord]Farseer[/color][/b].

        You should use it every time you need to do high healing on your whole group. In raids, pre-plan usage for the most dangerous parts of the fight.
        [pad]
    [/tab]

    [tab name="Swiftness" icon=spell_nature_ravenform]
        [minor-heading type=bar toc=false][symbol=wow-hero-talent-totemic] [color=venthyr]Totemic[/color] [color=shaman]Nature's Swiftness[/color] [icon name=spell_nature_ravenform type=round size=small inline=true color=c7][/icon][/minor-heading]

        [spell=378081] is an ability with a one-minute cooldown found in the capstone area of the Shaman class talents. It makes your next casted ability cost no mana and removes its cast time. Because the main drawback of [spell=1064] is its high mana cost you can use Swiftness as a way to get extra free Chain Heals over the course of a fight. You can also use it to speed up an emergency [spell=77472] in case someone is in danger of dying before you have time to finish a cast.

        The most important part of Swiftness however is the guaranteed [spell=1267068] you get when using it. Most of your Stormstreams during combat will come from using Swiftness on cooldown so it is very important that you don't hold the ability for too long or you will start losing out on valuable healing. The cooldown doesn't start until you consume the buff so don't forget to actually cast a spell as soon as possible after pressing it, you can hold the Stormstream proc for a bit longer if you don't need the healing right away.

        You can also use Nature's Swiftness to cast a damage spell instantly, but we don't recommend that.

        [minor-heading type=bar toc=false][symbol=wow-hero-talent-farseer] [color=necrolord]Farseer[/color] [color=shaman]Ancestral Swiftness[/color] [icon name=inv_ability_farseershaman_ancestralswiftness type=round size=small inline=true color=c7][/icon][/minor-heading]

        While playing [symbol=wow-hero-talent-farseer] [color=necrolord]Farseer[/color] this ability transforms into [spell=443454]. The main differences are a shorter cooldown, increasing the power on the ability you consume it with, and spawning an ancestor with every use. [b]You still need to talent into the baseline Nature's Swiftness from the class tree even if you have access to Ancestral Swiftness, otherwise it will not spawn an ancestor.[/b]

        With a reduced cooldown also comes extra Stormstream Totems, as every usage of Ancestral Swiftness will generate one the same way baseline Nature's Swiftness does. Combined with the ancestor that spawns from it this highlights the importance of using the spell on cooldown as much as possible even more.

        You should still generally consume Ancestral Swiftness with Chain Heal, but [spell=73920] or even damage spells in M+ can also be options.
        [pad]
    [/tab]

    [tab name="Spiritwalker's Grace" icon=spell_shaman_spiritwalkersgrace]
        [h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=spell_shaman_spiritwalkersgrace type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon][color=shaman] Spiritwalker's Grace [/color][/h3]

        [spell=79206] lets you cast abilities while moving for a short duration. This spell is very important to deal with forced movement scenarios where significant healing is still required.

        One quirk of the spell you can abuse is that whatever you are casting when the effect ends won't be immediately interrupted and can still be cast while moving. If you start one cast on the last second of the buff, you are free to finish that cast while moving even if the effect isn't present anymore. You can also activate it midway through a cast and start moving without interrupting yourself.
        [pad]
    [/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c7][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon] Restoration Shaman Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]

Some mechanics of Restoration are not super clear simply by reading their tooltips or observing their in-game behavior. If you want to get the most out of your gameplay you must understand how your abilities actually work. Here you will find detailed explanations on the intricacies of the most relevant abilities and talents.

[pad]
[tabs name="mechanics" uniform=true iconborders=true]
    [tab name="Stormstream Totem" icon=inv12_apextalent_shaman_stormstreamtotem]
        [h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=inv12_apextalent_shaman_stormstreamtotem type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon][color=shaman] Stormstream Totem [/color][/h3]

        Our apex talent [spell=1267068] comes in the form of a proc that improves our next cast of [spell=5394] giving it a high initial wave of healing, extra targets, and an overall healing increase while it is active. Stormstream Totem does not consume a charge of Healing Stream as every time it procs it will instantly restore one charge and also increase your maximum charges by one, so you should never lose out on casts of Healing Stream because of Stormstream.

        There are two ways to proc Stormstream: The first one and most reliable is by using [spell=378081] or [spell=443454]. Every cast of these spells will instantly generate one Stormstream so you should aim to use them as many times as possible during combat. The second way is a 6% chance every time you cast [spell=61295]. Do note that these Riptides have to be actually casted by you so free applications from [spell=382045] don't increase your chances.

        Once Stormstream procs you will get a 60 seconds buff that stacks up to two times, you can hold onto the buff for a decently long time in order to use it at the most appropriate moment but the longer you sit on it the more likely you are to lose out on Healing Stream casts due to not pressing the button at all. The two charges also make it very unlikely for you to miss out on procs by getting unlucky and generating one while already having one, you simply get the ability to use the ability back to back to drop two Stormstreams at the same time.

        For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-totemic] [color=venthyr]Totemic[/color] Stormstream will also heal one extra target at 30% power due to [spell=445035] and cast a free [spell=1064] from [spell=445034]. The spell also benefits from spec tree Healing Stream talents like [spell=1253099] and [spell=382482].

        This ability to stack up to two, the long duration of the buff, and the guaranteed proc from Swiftness gives you a lot of flexibility into how do you wanna use the totems and lets you align it properly with damage event for maximum value.

        The [spell=1267093] talent itself also increases all healing both Stormstream and Healing Stream do by 40%.
        [pad]
    [/tab]

    [tab name="Call of the Ancestors" icon=ability_racial_ancestralcall]
        [h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_racial_ancestralcall type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon][color=shaman] Call of the Ancestors [/color][/h3]

        The main feature of [symbol=wow-hero-talent-farseer] [b][color=necrolord]Farseer[/color][/b], [spell=443450] lets you summon ancestors by using [spell=73685] and [spell=443454]. These ancestors mimic your casts by using their own spells on the same target as you, increasing your healing.

        The ancestors have their own versions of the spells, so the power of their casts isn't affected by your talents. [spell=382309] mentions summoning an "Ancestral Spirit" on its description but this is just flavor text, the talent has no interaction with Farseer at all.

        [center][table class=grid width=50%]
    [tr background=c7]
        [td align=center]You Cast[/td]
        [td align=center]Your Ancestor Casts[/td]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td][spell=61295][/td]
        [td][spell=447415][/td]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td][spell=77472][/td]
        [td][spell=1223391][/td]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td][spell=73685][/td]
        [td][spell=447415][/td]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td][spell=1064][/td]
        [td][spell=447433][/td]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td][spell=5394][/td]
        [td][spell=447433][/td]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td][spell=73920][/td]
        [td][spell=447433][/td]
    [/tr]

        [td][spell=108280][/td]
        [td][spell=447433][/td]
    [/tr]

        [td][spell=470411][/td]
        [td][spell=447419][/td]
    [/tr]

    [/tr]

        [td][spell=51505][/td]

    [/tr]

        [td][spell=188443][/td]
        [td][spell=447425][/td]
    [/tr]
[/table][/center]
        [pad]
    [/tab]

    [tab name="Filler Spells" icon=inv_1115_shaman_chainheal]
        [h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=inv_1115_shaman_chainheal type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon][color=shaman] Filler Spells [/color][/h3]

        Restoration has two non-cooldown healing spells, [spell=77472] and [spell=1064]. Once all your short cooldowns are down these two spells are your only sources of healing. As of Midnight most talents that temporarily buff your next spell cast of these are gone or affect both spells equally. This means that when it comes time to cast a filler the two spells are competing with each other for your attention.

        There are some mechanics about [spell=1064] worth mentioning: As soon as the cast finishes, the increases from versatility, [spell=73685], and [spell=382039] are calculated right as the spell begins to jump. After each heal it will bounce to a new target reducing the amount of the heal by 30%. Each bounce gets increased by mastery, critical strike, [spell=974], and [spell=200076] independently of previous or subsequent jumps. [spell=1064] is a fully smart heal and it will always pick the targets that will make it do the most effective healing. [spell=114052] adds three extra jumps and changes the reduction between each jump from 30% to 10% but the same target can not be healed by multiple jumps so during M+ some of them will be wasted.

        For [spell=77472] the spell itself is a very simple single target heal on a very low mana cost. During [spell=114052] it will always critically strike and also heal a nearby ally for 50% of the amount. The extra hit from Ascendance counts as a full cast of the spell which means it can benefit from talents like [spell=16196] and [spell=382309] making it a very powerful effect.

        When it comes to numbers [spell=1064] is considerably stronger than [spell=77472] so it will be your default pick unless there are not enough injured targets to take full advantage of it or if your mana is running low, in those cases you should use [spell=77472]. During [spell=114052] both spells become much stronger but the difference remains the same: Chain Heal does much more healing overall while Healing Wave is better for spot healing and recovers more mana than what it costs to cast.

        For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-totemic] [color=venthyr]Totemic[/color] [spell=445034] will cast [spell=1064] completely free and with no cast time every time you use [spell=5394], [spell=108280], or [spell=98008] which is a very strong effect as it removes the main draw backs of the spell: its mana cost and cast time.
        [pad]
    [/tab]

    [tab name="Deeply Rooted Elements" icon=inv_misc_herb_liferoot_stem]
        [h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=inv_misc_herb_liferoot_stem type=round size=medium inline=true color=c7][/icon][color=shaman] Deeply Rooted Elements [/color][/h3]

        [spell=378270] gives you a 7% chance every time you apply a [spell=61295] to activate [spell=114052]. The talent does have bad luck protection; over time the number of procs you get should normalize, though it is still possible to get streaks one way or the other. Notably it is important to make the distinction that the talent can proc on every [spell=61295] [i]application[/i] not [i]cast[/i], so abilities that apply free [spell=61295]s like [spell=382045] can cause procs.

        Activations of [spell=114052] from [spell=378270] do benefit from [spell=462443] and also cause the initial healing.
        [pad]
    [/tab]
[/tabs]
[pad]

Our Restoration Shaman guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Restoration Shaman guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page, along with our list of [b]Related Guides[/b] just beneath the [i]Table of Contents[/i].


[tooltip name=NotesHighlight][color=q]Notes will appear here[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=StormstreamProcs][color=q]You will get a guaranteed proc every time you use Swiftness, and every Riptide cast has a low chance to generate one.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=RiptideTargets][color=q]You gain benefits from having more Riptides active, so pick targets that don't already have the hot from it.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=UnleashPrio][color=q]The most important part is that you use it often and get value out of the heal. The best spell to consume the buff is Chain Heal but you shouldn't worry too much about it and can simply use it on whatever spell you would normally cast.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=FarseerRain][color=q]Its easy to get value out of Healing Rain as you only need five targets inside of it and the area is big. The spell is worth casting even if you don't heal all targets for the whole duration.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=FarseerRainM+][color=q]You don't need to have all the group inside of rain all the time to make it worth using. Having a majority inside of it and using it to benefit from Deluge even as you consume Riptide buffs with Flow of the Tides makes it a very good pick.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=FarseerHst][color=q]While Healing Stream does decent healing and it is worth casting it is not a major source of healing and you will sometimes opt to not press it in order to better align your Stormstream Totems with damage.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=SwiftnessCooldown][color=q]The cooldown only starts after you consume the buff, so be sure you cast a spell that does as soon as possible after.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=FillerSelection][color=q]Picking between these spells will depend on how many targets need healing and how much mana do you have.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=SurgingTotem][color=q]Use Totemic Projection to move Surging Totem around as needed so you always have it below at least five targets.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=TotemicHst][color=q]The totem does a good amount of healing and also casts a free Chain Heal when you drop it. You should never waste its cooldown by being capped on stacks.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=Downpour][color=q]When playing Double Dip you will get two uses of Downpour for every Surging Totem. You can take your time in using it if there is nothing to heal yet, but you should not miss out on casts of it.[/color][/tooltip]
